scope: Repository producer-code inspection only. No external cache bytes, database, network, market outcome, or code changes.
strategy_layer: LEI Module E US S&P 500 market breadth input; this inspection tests input provenance, not returns or trading use.

code_proven.fact: The main full backfill reads a single SP500 fixture's symbol column, with no per-date membership filtering, then fetches each selected ticker's entire available US daily close history from Akshare/Sina using adjust='' (unadjusted). It resumes from pre-existing matrix columns without refreshing those columns; the date-by-symbol matrix is written to sp500_klines.parquet.

That backfill computes B20/B50/B200 as 100 times the count of same-day original closes strictly above each moving average divided by that horizon's eligible count. Moving averages use forward-filled internal gaps; a ticker is eligible only where original same-day close and moving average both exist. Each horizon requires at least 100 eligible tickers; dates without B20 are skipped and B50/B200 may remain null. Values are rounded to four decimals in JSON.

A separate us_breadth path loads the same fixture symbols and prioritizes the existing sp500_klines.parquet, then a user file, then five years of yfinance unadjusted Close. Its formula uses raw rolling windows without forward-fill, a distinct missing-price rule, and writes only the last max_points (default 1260) to the same JSON path. Therefore identical JSON path does not identify the producer or algorithm.

The tail-refresh path takes existing matrix columns, fetches three-month yfinance unadjusted Close, retains old values on overlaps, recomputes all JSON history using us_breadth's no-forward-fill algorithm, then overwrites both JSON and matrix. Thus a tail refresh can change the JSON algorithm without replacing historical matrix prices.

The timing conversion reads JSON's breadth_20/50/200 into b20/b50/b200, optionally joins advance/decline breadth from the matrix, and writes breadth_sp500.parquet after date deduplication. This path does not retain denominator, membership, source version, or available_at.

An alternative archived adjusted-price path takes ticker names from existing matrix columns, downloads yfinance auto_adjust=True closes into us_qfq_matrix.parquet, rejects series with <=250 observations or a daily fall of at least 40%, then computes breadth via an imported timing function and directly replaces timing breadth_sp500.parquet and sp500_klines.parquet. It does not write sp500_ma_breadth_history.json. The imported timing function lies outside this frozen contract, so its exact denominator and missing rules are not independently verified here.

The archived SQLite importer reads JSON values and recomputes eligible counts from the current matrix with forward-filled moving-average warmup. It uses the matrix's fixed column count for constituent_count and missing/coverage, copies JSON B values without reconciling formula or price revision, sets available_at equal to the row date, and stamps constant 'formal', 'complete', source, run and universe-version strings. It deletes prior SP500 rows before inserting into both snapshot and revision tables.

The distinct Round 5 fixture pipeline obtains the then-current Wikipedia list and gives every ticker effective_from=today. Its universe provider can filter historical membership if such effective intervals exist; its snapshot breadth computes each horizon over observed bars, records coverage, and sets available_at=as_of. This does not reconstruct former S&P 500 members.

unresolved_links: No cache file, run manifest, or fingerprint was read under this executor contract. Existing JSON, matrix, timing parquet, adjusted matrix, and database bytes cannot be attributed to one producer/version or proven mutually consistent from code alone.
No historical constituent identities with entry and exit effective dates, including departed names, are produced by the inspected current-list routes.
Historical warmup and adjusted prices for departed members, corporate-action revision vintages, and true data availability time are not established.

Timing parquet may be generated from unadjusted JSON or directly from adjusted matrix; a later timing conversion can overwrite the direct adjusted result. Exact present-cache lineage requires read-only fingerprints and value reconciliation by the controller.
qualification_implication: Local self-calculated breadth definitely has producer paths and previously audited numeric rows; that is separate from whether the values represent historical S&P 500 membership and were knowable at the decision date. Do not treat 'formal'/'complete' stamps or equal-date available_at as proof of historical qualification. No S01 market-effect test is justified from code provenance alone.
